vid_instagram_DewznmhMPWW.hook: Tracing a skull eye socket over a spoon held to the eye
vid_instagram_DewznmhMPWW.turn: Completing six different Halloween makeup looks using everyday tools
vid_instagram_DewznmhMPWW.whatHappens: Using everyday items like a spoon, tinfoil, and a fork, she completes six Halloween makeup looks from a skull to a clown.
checklist: Lock the camera at eye level in front of a plain wall with centered frontal light filling the face.
Cut briskly from stamping the tool on the face to the blended, finished Halloween look.

cues.cue: Press a spoon to the eye
cues.do: Open right on the action with a spoon pressed over the eye and a brush tracing the socket.
Coat an eyelash curler with liner and stamp it on the nose and lips to create symmetrical skull lines.
Hold the crumpled tinfoil close to the lens in front of the face so the red lipstick texture reads clearly.
Keep the main title fixed in the lower frame and swap only the second line to label each of the six hacks.
Place frontal lighting dead center to put circular catchlights in both eyes and keep the face free of shadows.

cues.cue: Turn head to show the cheek
cues.do: In a tight close-up against a plain wall, turn the head sideways on the reveal so the cheek makeup sits near center.

vid_instagram_DelxnyBTeSp.hook: Progress percentages for getting ready are shown above their heads.
vid_instagram_DelxnyBTeSp.turn: The woman finishes makeup, brings the man over, and waves.
vid_instagram_DelxnyBTeSp.whatHappens: With readiness counters above them, the man finishes first while the woman completes her makeup and brings him in to wave together.

beats.do: The man washes up behind her while the woman begins applying makeup with a hand mirror.
The woman looks into the hand mirror and applies under-eye makeup.
The man passes by changed into his clothes, while the woman applies mascara and contour.
The woman applies lip tint and touches up shine with a powder puff.
She removes her hair clip and spritzes spray onto her hair and neck.
She puts on an outer shirt, pulls the man in, and both wave at the camera.

checklist: Fix the camera slightly above eye level by a doorway.
Start with both people in pajamas staged diagonally in depth.
Have the partner return briefly in street clothes for the 100% beat, then step out.
Record short clips of each makeup step and the final outfit change.
Add floating percentage labels above both spots and cut tightly to the beat.

cues.do: Place readiness percentages above both heads to establish the comparison immediately without long text.
Stage her in the right foreground and him in the left midground so both fit clearly in vertical frame.
Look slightly up close to the lens while applying under-eye makeup so the step reads clearly.
Bring him back fully dressed at 100% while she is only at 60% to sharpen the speed contrast.
Shoot slightly above eye level to flatter the face and leave clean upper space for the floating numbers.
Jump-cut from pajamas into the cardigan and plum pants right as her counter hits 100%.
After calling him back from the room, reunite in the opening two-shot and wave both hands together.

vid_tiktok_7698354136579951905.hook: She shows her wet hair from behind.
vid_tiktok_7698354136579951905.turn: She shows her fully dried and voluminous hair.
vid_tiktok_7698354136579951905.whatHappens: From soaking wet to completely dry, a woman shows the drying stages of her long hair from behind.

beats.do: She runs her hands down her wet hair from behind.
She combs through her half-dried hair with both hands.
She runs her fingers down her mostly dried hair.
She sweeps through her fully dried hair to tidy it up.

checklist: Sit with your back to the camera in a plain dark shirt in front of a bright wall.
Fix the phone at shoulder height so your head and upper back fill the center of the frame.
Film four clips from soaking wet to fully dry while repeating the exact same two-handed hair shake.

cues.do: Open from behind shaking wet hair with the 0% dry text centered on the neck to promise a full drying progression.
Repeat the exact same two-handed hair shake across all four percentage cuts so only the drying change stands out.

cues.cue: Wear black before a white wall
cues.do: Wear a plain black shirt in front of a white wall so the brown hair ends and strand spacing read clearly.
Hold on the settled 75% dry hair where gaps between the thin lower strands show the black shirt underneath.
Lift the fully dry hair from underneath under an overhead light to create a bright horizontal band of shine.

checklist: Set a tripod facing a desk by a window with a laptop and drink in the foreground.
Start with playful banter from an off-camera questioner before asking the main question.
Act out physical side effects with facial expressions and hand gestures while explaining.
Pin the main title at the top and add punch-in zooms and inset diagrams in the edit.

cues.do: Start by answering an off-camera question while working at a laptop, keeping the main topic pinned at the top.
Place a laptop and drink cup in the foreground with curtains behind the speaker to add depth to a static shot.

cues.cue: Punch in on the teasing question
cues.do: Cut to a tighter crop right when the off-camera voice asks a teasing question to highlight her facial reaction.
Mimic the stiff upper lip while punching in with a sound effect so viewers instantly see the side effect.

cues.cue: Float a photo over the chest
cues.do: Place small square reference graphics over the chest area to show the scar location without hiding the speaker.

cues.cue: Light one side, dark the other
cues.do: Use soft daylight through the left sheer curtain to light the face and a dark right curtain for head contrast.

vid_instagram_DevulLUs4LU.hook: Sitting deadpan in a nasal strip before getting a haircut and shave
vid_instagram_DevulLUs4LU.turn: Slap transition reveals comical makeup first, then embroidered wedding outfits
vid_instagram_DevulLUs4LU.whatHappens: Getting ready for Mr Faisu's wedding with a haircut and shave, he fakes out with heavy makeup before a second slap reveals embroidered formalwear.
checklist: Shoot a deadpan front before shot in a casual tee and nasal strip.
Record quick multi-angle clips of the haircut and shave in the closet.
Match a cheek slap to a head turn revealing comical makeup first.
Use a second cheek slap to reveal the formal outfit, then pan to the mirror for a two-shot.

cues.cue: Open on a deadpan front shot
cues.do: Open on a deadpan front shot with a nasal strip and a yellow title above the head to set up the before state.
Shoot the haircut from three tight overhead angles and cut on the beat to speed up the prep montage.

cues.cue: Slap the cheek and turn left
cues.do: Grab the chin and slap the cheek toward screen left so the head turn carries seamlessly across the cut.

cues.cue: Cut to a shocked made-up face
cues.do: Delay the real outfit reveal by cutting first to heavy eyeshadow, dark lipstick, and a shocked expression.

cues.cue: Tilt your face to the top light
cues.do: After the second slap, angle the face toward the overhead closet light to sculpt the cheekbone and catch the embroidery.

cues.cue: Pan to the mirror, no cut
cues.do: Pan straight into the wall mirror without cutting to frame both friends in full traditional outfits.

vid_tiktok_7697448995152596255.hook: brushing teal paint down her face
vid_tiktok_7697448995152596255.whatHappens: She paints a teal stripe down the center of her face, then transforms into an otherworldly alien creature on the beat drop.
checklist: Lock the phone on a tripod with normal room light and stand dead-centre in a plain hoodie.
Lip-sync to the track while painting one continuous mint stripe from forehead to neck.
Dip your head down with eyes closed right before the chorus lyric begins.
Start in the exact same spot with your head dipped and lift it on the chorus beat to match the cut.

cues.do: Touch the bright mint brush straight to the centre of the forehead in the first second to build curiosity right away.
Close the eyes and tilt the chin up while pulling one unbroken stripe from forehead to neck in time with the song.
Lock the phone on a tripod with the painted stripe on the vertical centre line so the before and after align cleanly.

cues.cue: Dip and lift at the chorus
cues.do: Dip the head just before the chorus and lift it in the exact same spot after the cut for a seamless costume reveal.
Keep the front key light on the face after the cut, but flood the white doors behind with mint light to match the look.

cues.cue: Look up on the high note
cues.do: Tilt the head and look upward on the high vocal note so the front light catches the pink lenses and forehead ridges.

beats.do: She applies and peels off eyebrow tattoos, then puts on false lashes.

She pats with a puff and blends contour across her face with a brush.
She dots stick blush onto her cheeks and blends it with a brush.
She sets the skin with powder, then lines and colors her lips.
She applies lip gloss and strikes poses to show off her makeup.

checklist: Mount the camera at eye level directly in front of you.
Film only the exact moments each cosmetic product touches the skin.
Trim out dead time and connect each step using brisk jump cuts.

cues.do: Opens the routine with an inviting hand wave and an everyday work prep caption.
Peels off the eyebrow transfer paper to reveal the realistic brow shape underneath.
Soft frontal natural light casts even highlights across the forehead and cheekbones.
Rapid jump cuts trim each makeup step down to just the essential contact moments.

cues.cue: Put your eyes on the top third
cues.do: Positions the camera at mirror height, placing the eyes precisely along the upper third.

cues.cue: Frame your jaw to show off
cues.do: Frames the finished look with playful hand gestures and confident facial expressions.

tiktok_7693273932794793247.hook: She introduces her skincare routine step by step.
tiktok_7693273932794793247.turn: She peels off the gel mask to reveal glowing skin.
tiktok_7693273932794793247.whatHappens: A woman goes through a skincare routine with pads, creams, and a gel mask, then peels it off to show glowing, hydrated skin.

beats.do: Wipe your face, neck, and décolleté with a toner pad, then show the pad.
Apply serum to the cheeks to absorb, then apply a stick balm to the neck.
Dab the stick balm on the lips and present the gua sha neck cream tube.
Massage your jawline, neck, and chest using the gua sha applicator tube.
Apply the top and bottom pieces of the pink gel mask to your face.
Peel off the transparent gel mask and pat your glowing skin to show it off.

checklist: Wear a bandeau top and hair band to expose the face and clavicle lines clearly.
Place an open palm behind bottles to lock camera focus onto product labels.
Punch in to an extreme close up when serums drip across the cheek.
Face the key light after peeling the mask to showcase glass reflection on skin.

cues.cue: Show the glow down to the collarbone
cues.do: Showcase skin radiance down to the decollete to immediately expand the scope of the skincare routine.

cues.cue: Hold the used pad to the lens
cues.do: Hold the used toner pad close to the camera to visually demonstrate residue removal.

cues.cue: Put a palm behind the bottle
cues.do: Place an open palm behind the bottle to lock camera autofocus directly onto the product label.

cues.cue: Center the tube below the chin
cues.do: Place the product tube precisely along the vertical centreline below the face for immediate eye contact.

cues.cue: Light the face from the front
cues.do: Position front lighting to bounce specular catchlights off forehead and clavicle for a glass finish.

checklist: Sit facing soft front daylight and mount the phone steady at eye level.
Start with a playful finger wag toward the lens to show the bare face.
Layer red corrector and concealer visibly before blending one eye at a time.
Switch hands when applying mascara so your arm never blocks the camera.
End by looking straight into the lens and blowing a two-handed kiss.

cues.cue: Wag a finger at the lens
cues.do: Open by wagging a finger right at the lens before smiling. Start with an immediate gesture instead of a slow intro.

cues.cue: Dab red corrector on dark spots
cues.do: Apply bright red corrector directly onto dark circles and around the mouth early on to build anticipation for the blend.
Layer two shades of concealer over the red base before blending so viewers stay to see how the stark patches disappear.
Keep the face centered and blend one eye completely first to create a live before and after comparison in one frame.
Sit facing soft front daylight behind the phone so neither cheek falls into shadow and true skin coverage reads clearly.

cues.cue: Cut only at the tissue grab
cues.do: Cut only once when grabbing a tissue and leave all blending uncut in real time to prove the coverage uses no filters.

cues.cue: Use your left hand on that eye
cues.do: Switch the mascara wand to the left hand for the opposite eye so the arm never crosses the frame or blocks the lashes.
Finish the full transformation by blowing a two handed kiss to the lens, echoing the opening hand gesture.

She adds blush to her cheeks and carefully draws eyeliner.

checklist: Record a quick snippet of the finished look first.
Film the bare-faced start while removing hair curlers.
Apply makeup in steps under even front light while looking into the lens.
Conclude with a confident smile and a kiss gesture toward camera.

cues.do: Flash the finished makeup look in the opening second to set visual expectations.
Place caption below the chest so it does not obscure the face or makeup tools.
Frame subject centrally from bust to crown to maintain comfortable eye contact.
